Order 
This Miscellaneous Appeal, under Section 173(1) of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, has been filed against Award dated 13.09.2013 passed by Member, I Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Gwalior (M.P.) in Claim Case No. No.57/2013 for enhancement of compensation.

entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. The factum of accident and liability of parties is not in dispute.
It is the case of appellant that on 11.10.2011, he was standing behind the tractor by the side of road.
At that time, driver of offending Jeep bearing registration No.UP75-J-5010 dashed the tractor and trolley by driving the vehicle in a rash and negligent manner.
The offending vehicle also got burnt in the accident and appellant suffered grievous injuries on both his legs and chest.

During NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-GWL:11040 treatment, appellant underwent three major operations and ultimately his both legs were amputated from above the knee.
Appellant remained hospitalized for a period of 17 days.
3. Challenging the insufficiency of compensation amount, it is submitted by counsel for appellant that it is the case of appellant that he was a skilled mason and was earning Rs.400/- per day.

However, in paragraph 19 of the Award, although it is held that appellant has successfully proved Kamlesh Rathore vs Hariom @ Dabish Jha on 7 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/160622884/
1 that he was a labourer

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: but held that even if he is treated as semi-skilled labourer, still his daily income would have been Rs.100/- and ultimately it was held that monthly income of appellant was Rs.4000/-.
The Claims Tribunal had also held that appellant had suffered 100% permanent disability in both his legs.
It is submitted that when the claimant has failed to prove his income by leading cogent evidence, then notification issued under the Minimum Wages Act can be treated as guiding factor.

4. Considered the submissions made by counsel for appellant.
5.

The Claims Tribunal has held that appellant has failed to prove that he was earning Rs.400/- per day and after assessing the evidence which was led by appellant has held that the monthly income of the appellant on 11.10.2011 was Rs.4,000/-.

It is well established principle of law that when claimants fail to prove the actual income of the injured or deceased, then the guidelines issued under the Minimum Wages Act can be taken as a guiding factor.
As per the notification issued under the Minimum Wages Act, the monthly income of an unskilled labourer on 11.10.2011 was Rs.4,545/-.

Therefore, it is held that the monthly income of appellant was Rs.4,545/- and not Rs.4000/- as held by the Claims Tribunal and accordingly, claimant/appellant is entitled to the following compensation amount:-
